title: The Altitude Where Axioms Dissolve Into Sky

features.name: the proof that forgot its conclusion
features.desc-on-touch: A structure built of pure logic that ascends and ascends and then stops—the capstone is missing. The architecture continues in the sky as invisible weight, and anything placed underneath it immediately becomes theoretically true.

features.name: the dissolving statement
features.desc-on-touch: Letters written in water at the sky-boundary. As you read them, the meaning rises away. What remains is the shape of meaning, the space where a fact was true once, before altitude made it obsolete.

features.name: the wind that proves nothing
features.desc-on-touch: A current that carries argument into silence. Everything that arrives here is subjected to the test of sky—and the sky has no axioms. What cannot float is set down gently as metaphor.

features.name: the axiom made visible
features.desc-on-touch: A crystal line in the air, the shape of a rule held by nothing. You can see through it. It is dissolving the way ice dissolves at altitude—upward into the humidity it came from.

inscription: here the rules learned that sky has no grammar

file.name: Proof_That_Sought_Its_Own_Refutation_Incomplete.txt
file.note: A mathematical argument that reaches its own altitude and then pages go blank. The final lines are written in air. The corruption has made the blankness more convincing than any conclusion.

reverie.title: REVERIE — dusk on the rooftop, the argument
narr: you stood with her where the proof ran out of altitude.
she said: the sky doesn't care if you're right.
neither of you finished the conversation.
now you can't remember which side you were on.
the meaning dissolved the way she was dissolving.
